clue.text: Are audible errors a clue to this poet?

indicators.note: errors are mistakes, things set wrong, so the letters of 'are audible' are to be set in a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle asks whether mistakes you can hear point the way to a particular poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'errors' signals the anagram: ARE AUDIBLE rearranges into the French poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Baudelaire was the French poet of Les Fleurs du mal.

clue.text: Fury expressed in dialect, of course

indicators.note: the name is pressed out from inside the words that follow, running across 'dialect, of'

explanation.surface: Anger comes out in a regional way of speaking, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressed in' signals letters hidden across 'diALECT Of'. 'Fury' looks like plain anger, but it is one of the three Furies of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecto is one of the three Erinyes, the avenging goddesses of Greek myth.

clue.text: No Haydn I played recalled Hungarian pianist

indicators.note: music that is played is performed, so these letters are performed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Hungarian pianist recalls refusing to play any Haydn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' signals the anagram of NO HAYDN, giving DOHNANY, with I kept at the end; 'recalled' is a link, the pianist remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernő Dohnányi was a celebrated Hungarian pianist and composer.

clue.text: It's all autobiographical, said Borges

parts.note: Borges remarked that all writing of this kind is autobiographical; the missing word in his saying is the subject

explanation.walkthrough: The clue completes a saying of the Argentine writer Jorge Luis Borges: 'All ... is autobiographical'. The printed enumeration (5,1,4) does not fit; the grid takes one ten-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Borges's remark was about the whole body of written works, which is the word missing from his quotation.

clue.text: Getting soaked at Betjeman's teashop?

explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city; Betjeman's poem title gives the phrase, and taken literally the same words describe a soak.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying in a tub is getting soaked; John Betjeman's poem 'In a Bath Teashop' sets its lovers in a tearoom in the English spa city.

clue.text: Bayly's green isle

parts.note: the songwriter Thomas Haynes Bayly, like many poets, used the old poetic name for Ireland, the emerald isle

explanation.definitionFit: The poetic name for Ireland, often called the green isle in song.

clue.text: City's familiar name for Alexander's sister

definitions.text: City's familiar name for Alexander's sister

parts.words: City's familiar name for Alexander's sister
parts.note: Thessaloniki was named after Thessalonike, half-sister of Alexander the Great, and was long known by a shorter everyday form

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek port named for Alexander's half-sister Thessalonike was commonly called by this shortened name in English.

clue.text: Ruralist writer said to be piling up prepared meat

parts.note: massing means gathering or piling up
ham is cured, prepared pork

explanation.surface: A country author is rumoured to be stockpiling cooked meats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' is a link telling you the writer's name sounds like the two words strung together. H. J. Massingham wrote on English rural life.
explanation.definitionFit: H. J. Massingham was an English author writing about the countryside and farming traditions.

clue.text: She was seen by Lee as a rival queen

definitions.text: She was seen by Lee as a rival queen

parts.words: She was seen by Lee as a rival queen
parts.note: Nathaniel Lee's tragedy The Rival Queens pits Alexander's wife against Statira

explanation.definitionFit: In Nathaniel Lee's play The Rival Queens, Alexander the Great's first wife is one of the two rivals.

clue.text: He's curiously taken by Middle Eastern bread in Aramaic Bible

indicators.note: being taken by the bread means sitting inside it

parts.note: pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the letters of 'He's' come in an odd order

explanation.surface: A man is oddly drawn to pitta bread while studying an ancient scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' is the anagram signal on the man's contraction, and 'taken by' means held within the flatbread. 'in' links wordplay to the scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peshitta is the standard Syriac translation of the scriptures, Syriac being a dialect of Aramaic.

clue.text: Early Belgian composer a very short distance inside French wood

indicators.note: inside places the distance within the French word for wood

parts.note: bois is French for wood
an inch is a tiny length, as in 'not moving an inch'

explanation.surface: A composer from the Low Countries is placed a hair's breadth into a French forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal. 'Belgian' is fair though Binchois worked at the Burgundian court: his birthplace, Mons, is now in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilles Binchois, born in Mons, was a fifteenth-century Burgundian composer from what is now Belgium.

clue.text: Madman, a mere description from E. L. Doctorow?

definitions.text: a mere description from E. L. Doctorow

explanation.walkthrough: A mere is a lake: Doctorow's title Loon Lake uses the word as the lake's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is a lunatic; in Doctorow's novel Loon Lake the word describes a mere, a small lake.

clue.text: Schneitzhoeffer's singular nudge to Chopin?

parts.note: Schneitzhoeffer scored the 1832 ballet whose title is the singular of the later Chopin ballet Les Sylphides

explanation.definitionFit: Jean Schneitzhoeffer wrote the music for the Romantic ballet La Sylphide, a singular counterpart to the Chopin ballet of spirits.

clue.text: Not accepting moral law, yet opposed to revolutionary Minoan

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the letters of 'Minoan' are turned about

explanation.surface: Someone who rejects morality also sets himself against a radical from ancient Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' is the anagram signal, not a description of the Cretan; 'yet' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinomian holds that faith frees Christians from obligation to observe moral rules.

clue.text: Author supporting cardinal points is a recorder of current events

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means standing below, so the author goes beneath the points

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four cardinal compass points
an author is a writer

explanation.surface: A writer backing the compass directions turns out to be a chronicler of the day's happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts WRITER under NEWS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who writes reports on the latest happenings records current events.

clue.text: Unreliable Greek church historian reveals waste vehicle going from South to North America

parts.note: South (America) shares the word America with North America later in the clue: SA
a bin is the vessel that carries rubbish
the US stands for the North American country

explanation.surface: A dubious historian reports a rubbish truck travelling between the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going from South to North America' sets the bin between the two continents' abbreviations, the word America serving both.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabinus of Heraclea compiled acts of church councils that Socrates Scholasticus criticised as partial and inaccurate.

clue.text: Unnecessary fuss by Shakespeare features this newly-wed

definitions.text: Unnecessary fuss by Shakespeare features this newly-wed

parts.words: Unnecessary fuss by Shakespeare features this newly-wed
parts.note: unnecessary fuss is Much Ado About Nothing, whose confirmed bachelor finally marries Beatrice

explanation.definitionFit: From Shakespeare's Benedick, the word came to mean a long-time bachelor who has newly married.

clue.text: A BBC Director-General, they say, gets garland from Herbert

indicators.note: they say signals that the name is heard, standing for a word sounding the same

parts.note: John Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC

explanation.surface: A broadcasting chief, rumour has it, receives a floral tribute from a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Reith founded the BBC's public-service ethos; his name sounds like the ring of flowers that George Herbert's poem 'A Wreath' is titled after.
explanation.definitionFit: George Herbert's poem 'A Wreath' is a circular chain of verse, like a ring of flowers.

clue.text: He makes his rounds every evening while you and I see the once a week (O Henry, Four Million)

definitions.text: He makes his rounds every evening while you and I see the once a week (O Henry, Four Million)

parts.words: He makes his rounds every evening while you and I see the once a week (O Henry, Four Million)
parts.note: a quotation from O. Henry's collection The Four Million with a gap for the animal in the idiom 'see the ...', meaning to see life

explanation.walkthrough: To 'see the elephant' is an American idiom for seeing the world; O. Henry's sentence leaves the animal out for you to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to see the ...' uses this big beast to mean gaining worldly experience.

clue.text: Burke announced late transport to these fields

definitions.text: Burke announced late transport to these fields

parts.words: Burke announced late transport to these fields
parts.note: the fields of the blessed in Greek myth, where the dead are transported, named in a passage by Edmund Burke

explanation.definitionFit: The Elysian Fields were the paradise of Greek myth to which heroes were carried after death.

clue.text: Poet, unlike his subject, Thangbrand the Priest ("Short of stature, large of limb")?

definitions.text: Poet, unlike his subject, Thangbrand the Priest ("Short of stature, large of limb")

parts.words: Poet, unlike his subject, Thangbrand the Priest ("Short of stature, large of limb")
parts.note: in The Saga of King Olaf the priest is described as short; the poet's surname read as two words means a tall man

explanation.walkthrough: The American poet's surname splits into LONG FELLOW, the opposite of his short priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow wrote The Saga of King Olaf, which describes Thangbrand.

clue.text: Is the fashion returning for biblical land?

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for fashion is read backwards

parts.note: the mode is the current fashion, as in à la mode

explanation.surface: A question whether a style is coming back, framed around a place in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Edom was the kingdom south of the Dead Sea, home of Esau's descendants in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Widdershins author may bring tears to our eyes

definitions.text: may bring tears to our eyes

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Onions wrote the ghost-story collection Widdershins; peeling bulb vegetables makes eyes water.

clue.text: Quixotic story (the butler did it)

parts.note: the butler is Samuel Butler, who wrote a mock-heroic poem modelled on Don Quixote; the phrase plays on the detective cliché

explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler's satirical poem follows a Presbyterian knight on Quixote-like adventures.

clue.text: Macbeth character in Rattigan play?

explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish thane in Macbeth bears this name, and Terence Rattigan's play about T. E. Lawrence is titled after his alias.

clue.text: Interior curve of arch marks the entrances?

explanation.definitionFit: The intrados is the inner, lower curve of an arch; in an arched doorway that curve outlines the opening you walk through.

clue.text: Conspirator named Brutus

parts.note: in Julius Caesar the conspirators include a second Brutus besides Marcus, known by his first name

explanation.definitionFit: Decius Brutus is one of the plotters against Caesar in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Try "Secs.", Min." variation for inflectional fusion

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters of the three words are changed in order

explanation.surface: An instruction to vary seconds and minutes, as if timing a linguistic process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' signals the anagram of TRY SECS MIN.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics, syncretism is the merging of distinct grammatical case forms into one.
